Goal 3: Ensure Funding for Recycling and Solid Waste Management

Apply host fees collected from Eagle Point to support convenience center operations, recycling
and waste reduction, education and enforcement, and household hazardous waste collection
events.

Continue to charge residents delivering bagged household waste to the convenience centers,
offering an incentive for those that also recycle and charging more for excess bags.
Monitor the availability of grants, especially for recycling, and apply for those applicable.

Explore other funding sources for recycling and solid waste management and implement as
feasible and necessary to maintain or expand infrastructure or programs.

Continue to collect solid waste and recyclable from residents at the convenience centers,
committing the resources necessary to meet demand.
Emphasize source reduction and reuse. Encourage private haulers to offer recycling. Provide support and encourage businesses to recycle. Expand recycling
Encourage private haulers to offer recycling to their customers.

Work with private haulers to determine what support would be needed to cost-effectively provide
recycling to customers and provide, when possible.

Evaluate the option of requiring private haulers to offer recycling to their customers as part of a
permit requirement and implement if feasible.

Work with businesses, industry, and institutions to determine what support would be needed to
initiate or expand recycling and provide, when possible.

Work with processors and end users to expand the type of material collected for recycling at
convenience centers.

Continue to incentivize recycling by offering a lower rate for disposal of bagged household garbage
for those that recycle.

Evaluate the need for a facility to consolidate, transfer, and/or process recyclables collected in the
County.

If additional capacity is needed to cost effectively get recyclables to processors or end users,
develop, potentially in conjunction with surrounding local governments and/or a private partner.

Provide in-kind funding and support to KFCB who will continue to lead outreach and education,
litter prevention, recycling, and waste reduction efforts in the County.

Maintain and promote KFCB’s website (www.keepforsythcountybeautiful.org) and continue to use
as central repository for all information about waste reduction, recycling, and litter prevention in the
County.

Continue to educate residents at events and in schools, clubs, and community, neighborhood, and
organization meetings about waste reduction and recycling and litter prevention.
Operate recycling and composting demonstration sites.

Increase use of social media to promote waste reduction and recycling throughout the planning
period to reach a broader audience.

Collaborate with Eagle Point, private haulers, and other service providers to assist in outreach and
education on recycling and responsible solid waste management.
